newsitem.title: SPAIN: Caller says Basque separatists shot wrong man.
newsitem.headline: Caller says Basque separatists shot wrong man.

text.p: A caller claiming to speak on behalf of Basque separatist ETA guerrillas said Tuesday's attack in which militant socialist Javier Perez was shot and wounded in the head had been "a mistake", officials said on Wednesday.
The caller told an emergency dispatcher in the northern Basque region in Spain that Perez had been confused with someone else.

Officials and politicians reacted angrily to the suggestion that any attack by the rebels, who have killed some 800 people in their drive for an independent Basque state, could be considered an error.

"The sarcasm supposed by saying it had been a mistake is in no way acceptable," Basque interior counsellor Juan Maria Atutxa told journalists. "There aren't mistakes, the only intent is to kill and torture."
Perez, 37, was shot in the back of the neck in the Basque city of Bilbao while he was walking his dog. Hospital officials said the bullet missed his brain and he would recover.
A Socialist party official said Perez often acted as a security guard at party functions and could have been mistaken for a member of Spain's security forces.
